newsitem.title: USA: Court upholds Pa. Gov's right to name board -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds Pa. Gov's right to name board -- paper.

text.p: A federal court ruled that Pennsylvania Gov. Tom Ridge has an unrestricted right to appoint and remove board members to Delaware River Port Authority, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Thursday.
The Third U.S. Court of Appeals ruled unanimously against Max Pievsky, a Philadelphia Democrat removed from the DRPA board by the Republican governor in January.
Pievsky had asked the court to allow him to serve out the remainder of his five-year term, but the court instead affirmed a lower court ruling against Pievsky.
The court said board members serve at the governor's pleasure.
The DRPA board consists of eight commissioners from Pennsylvania and eight from New Jersey. The governors of each state appoint six of the members.
In the secondary market Thursday, the agency's FGIC 5.3s of 2010 were being offered at a 5.35 percent net. JJ Kenny Inc priced the bonds at a 5.45 percent yield at the close Wednesday.
